messages:
michael: heads up — user reported SSO errors after last night's key rotation, SCIM provisioning 400s and a handful of failures when exchanging SAML assertions for sessions
hina: details? error message? which customer/IdP?
michael: tenant: acme-corp, IdP: Okta. Logs show 'invalid signature: rsa_padding_check_failed' and in auth-proxy: 'signature verification failed (expected RS256)'. SCIM calls return 400 with correlation id `c2f7-9a`
ryan: that padding error smells like alg mismatch (PS256 vs RS256) rather than KMS corruption. Did KMS switch to RSA-PSS key policy during rotate?
michael: possible. Devops bot announced a rekey at 03:10 UTC: `devops-bot: rotated kms alias projects/redwood/keys/idp-signing-key` — but no extra notes about alg change
devops-bot: automated note — KMS keyrotation completed for alias idp-signing-key at 2026-03-20T03:10:12Z (key-id: projects/redwood/keys/abc123). No permission changes.
hina: Okta can be configured to sign with PS256 if the app wants it, and some newer toolchains prefer PS. But our verifier service currently only accepts RS256 (we still call it RSASSA-PKCS1_v1_5).
security-oncall: customer impact: P2 (SCIM failures, SSO fallback to manual login). Can we confirm assertion alg in incoming SAML?
ryan: pulled raw SAML from acme logs: `<ds:SignatureMethod Algorithm=\"http://www.w3.org/2007/05/xmldsig-more#rsa-pss\"/>` — that's PS256. Our metadata had `rsa-sha256` expectation.
michael: that matches the padding error. Okta apparently switched signing algorithm on their end when they refreshed IdP certs. Need to either accept PS256 or ask Okta to change to RS256. Which is quicker?
hina: short term: we can add PS256 verifier support to auth-proxy and run a canary behind a feature flag. Long term: probably support both but require strict audit.
ryan: PR path: add `RSASSA-PSS` branch to signature verifier, fallback order: RS256 -> PS256. Canary on dedicated auth instances for 2 hours then toggle. I can draft patch.
michael: also need audit log entries for which alg was used per assertion (so we can track IdPs that send PS). Add a trace field `idp_signature_alg` to auth audit logs.
hina: agree. Also cross-check KMS key: PS requires different padding use but same RSA key can be used; KMS policy shouldn't have changed. Still, export a public key and run `openssl pkeyutl` verify to be safe.
ryan: quick check commands I ran: `gcloud kms keys versions get-public-key 1 --key=idp-signing-key --output-file=pub.pem` and then `openssl pkeyutl -verify -in sig.bin -inkey pub.pem -sigopt rsa_padding_mode:pss -pkeyopt digest:sha256`. That verifies with PSS settings.
michael: good. Who's owning the rollout?
ryan: I'll own the verifier change and canary. Timeline: patch today, canary in staging tonight, prod canary tomorrow morning.
hina: I'll add the audit log field + a one-off migration to backfill logs for last 24h during the canary window so we can correlate failed scim requests with alg used.
security-oncall: also open a compliance note: we need to record that some IdPs send PS256 and that we accepted it for compatibility. Add a KMS audit event referencing the rotation id and time.
michael: filed INC-2026-142 on PagerDuty, cc'ing Okta SRE to see if they pushed a config change: @okta-sre can you confirm whether any global signing alg update occurred for acme-corp or auto-rotation of alg policy?
okta-sre: ack — checking with tenant ops now. Preliminary: Okta rotated IdP certs for several orgs; default app setting is 'auto' and some customers got PS256 after rotation. We'll follow up in 20m.
hina: temporary mitigation for SCIM: add retry with backoff and fallback to service account token (manual) for provisioning-only flows until verifier supports PS. But that is risky and should be opt-in per tenant.
ryan: actually adding PS support in verifier is low risk if we keep strict validation: require exact audience and issuer, check cert chain, only accept PS for IdPs we've seen successfully verify in staging. Canary first.
michael: ok. Action items: ryan -> implement verifier PS support + canary (owner) ; hina -> add audit field + backfill script ; security-oncall -> update incident ticket with compliance note and KMS rotation correlation ; okta-sre -> confirm if rotation toggled algs.
devops-bot: deploy pipeline queued: auth-proxy/patch-pss (CI green) -> canary group `auth-canary-2` (manual approval)
ryan: pushing PR: `feat(auth): support RSASSA-PSS (PS256) signature verification behind feature flag` — link: https://git.internal/reviews/2251
hina: backfill script: `python tools/backfill_idp_alg.py --since 2026-03-19T00:00Z --out backfill-20260319.csv` (will run post-canary)
michael: communication plan: tell affected customers we saw IdP signing alg changes after IdP cert rotation; we're deploying compatibility patch. ETA prod canary 2026-03-21 09:00 UTC.
security-oncall: any further vuln surface? PSS is stronger padding-wise, so accepting it is not a downgrade. But any change in acceptance increases attack surface if we mishandle verification parameters. Ensure `sigopt` params are explicit.
ryan: noted — will set explicit `rsa_padding_mode=pss` and `mgf1md=sha256` in verifier lib, no defaults.
okta-sre: update — confirmed: acme-corp's app was set to 'auto' and Okta default now prefers PSS when certs are RSA keys that support it. They can flip back but many customers will prefer PSS.
michael: final: proceed with canary + audit backfill + customer comms. Keep this thread updated with canary metrics (error rate, latency, scim success rate).
hina: I'll post backfill output and a short note in the incident ticket once done.
ryan: canary results: auth-canary-2 ran for 2h (09:00-11:00 UTC), no regressions, PS256 assertions validated, SCIM error rate for acme-corp dropped to 0.2% from 8%. Rolling to wider pool at 11:30 UTC.
michael: thanks all. closing incident when rollout completes and Okta confirms config guidance. :thumbsup:
